The key bottleneck is the trade-off between sophisticated phase-aware scoring (slow but thorough) and fast static scoring (fast but potentially suboptimal). Instead of tracking removal progress, the algorithm uses graph-aware static weights (determined once by CV and bridge_ratio) to balance structural and spectral importance. The innovation is a multiplicative fusion strategy: (1) structural component combines normalized core and dampened betweenness (sqrt) to target bridges, scaled by bridge_ratio; (2) spectral component uses quadratic eigenvector amplification (eigen^2) instead of exponential, providing late-stage dominance naturally when eigenvector values are high; (3) these components are multiplied (not harmonically meaned) to ensure nodes must excel in both dimensions to rank highly, naturally filtering out nodes that are only locally or only spectrally important; (4) a simple division by (1 + clustering) provides redundancy penalty. This avoids conditionals inside the loop, eliminates progress calculation overhead, replaces expensive exp() with multiplication, and maintains the early/late balance through the opposing dampening (sqrt) and amplification (square) operations.
